latin_incipit: Coelum est corpus simplex, non compositum ex materia et forma.
english_translation: Heaven is a simple body, not composed of matter and form.
charge: Averroes defends the Aristotelian doctrine that the heavens are composed of a simple, fifth element (aether) without terrestrial matter and form.
defense: Pico accepts this to uphold the distinction between incorruptible heavens and corruptible terrestrial bodies, key to medieval cosmology.
exegesis: Contrary to terrestrial bodies, the heavens are simple, immutable substances. Pico registers this to uphold celestial incorruptibility, a key cosmological distinction.

scholar_citations.quote: The heavens are composed of a fifth element (aether) which is eternal and incorruptible, unlike the four terrestrial elements.
The simplicity and immutability of the heavens follows necessarily from their eternal circular motion.

scholar_citations.work: Scholasticism and Medieval Metaphysics in Pico
scholar_citations.quote: The incorruptibility of the heavens was essential to medieval theodicy and theories of divine immutability.

notes: Defends the coherence of medieval two-tiered cosmology (celestial vs. terrestrial). Challenged by modern physics but important to Renaissance thought.
